identity.name: Master Ultra Thin Moon
identity.one_liner: A slim automatic dress watch with a moonphase display, positioned as JLC's standard-catalog entry point into its own complicated-watchmaking history.

narrative.story: Jaeger-LeCoultre has built moonphase watches across most of its history since its 1833 founding in Le Sentier, and the manufacture makes its own movements and components for other Richemont-group brands as well as itself. The Master Ultra Thin Moon takes that in-house depth and applies it to a simple, legible complication in a thin automatic case rather than reserving moonphases for limited or boutique-only pieces — the moon disc sits at six o'clock beneath a conventional three-hand-and-date layout.
narrative.collector_notes: Confirm the moon disc's synodic accuracy claim on the specific generation — JLC has offered both standard (roughly one day of drift every 122 years) and higher-precision moonphase modules across different Master lines, and the two are not interchangeable in the same case.
